architect_instruction: Preserve the existing process_data behavior and all existing tests. Add a new function detect_plateaus(values, min_length=2) to src/pipeline.py. It must accept a list of values and return a list of dictionaries describing consecutive runs of equal values whose length is at least min_length. Each returned dictionary must contain exactly the keys value, start_index, end_index, and length, and results must preserve original occurrence order. For example, detect_plateaus([3, 3, 1, 2, 2, 2, 4], 2) must return [{'value': 3, 'start_index': 0, 'end_index': 1, 'length': 2}, {'value': 2, 'start_index': 3, 'end_index': 5, 'length': 3}]. An empty list must return an empty list. Runs shorter than min_length must be omitted. If min_length is less than 1, raise ValueError. Add meaningful unit tests in tests/test_pipeline.py covering multiple qualifying plateaus, runs that are too short, a plateau spanning the entire input, min_length=1, empty input, and invalid min_length values. Preserve all existing functionality and tests, add no external dependencies, run the complete test suite, and create a new git commit only if every test passes.
reasoning_summary: Added detect_plateaus to src/pipeline.py with validation for min_length < 1 and linear-scan consecutive run detection returning the required keys and preserving occurrence order. Preserved existing process_data. Added comprehensive unit tests in tests/test_pipeline.py covering all specified edge cases while preserving existing test_process_data.
